claim: Extrinsic IO functions cover stdout printing and stdin byte reads only.

receipts.text: The @io_print_char extrinsic functions takes an IO value

claim: IO is by an IO handle passed to main; functions without it are pure; IO is asynchronous.

receipts.text: Any function that does not get passed a reference to an IO handle is pure (i.e. does not interact with the outside world).

claim: IO cannot be forked or dropped, so exactly one IO handle exists.

receipts.text: This means that at any point in the execution of a Vine program, there is exactly one IO handle, so all IO operations are ordered.

claim: Types are linear by default; ? * + annotations choose droppable/forkable.

receipts.text: By default, the type is neither forkable nor droppable; its values must be used exactly once.

claim: Vine has traits, generic implementations and implementation parameters.

receipts.text: The advantage of using traits instead of just defining individual functions for types is that, with traits, one can abstract over any type that has an implementation of a certain trait.

claim: Vine has enums with pattern matching (algebraic data types).

receipts.text: An enum is a type with a fixed set of variants. An enum value is one of those variants.

claim: The inverse feature is described as only possible due to interaction nets; the docs page calls itself bad.

receipts.text: Note: This page is bad and should feel bad.

claim: Inverse enables 'time travel' (backwards data flow) such as single-pass sub_min.

receipts.text: Since an inverted variable flows “backwards in time”

claim: Compiler pipeline emits Ivy nets, one per stage.

receipts.text: The emitter then converts each specialization of the VIR into a collection of Ivy nets, one for each stage.

claim: Compiler uses Stacked Flow Graphs as intermediate representation.

receipts.text: The Vine compiler uses Stacked Flow Graphs (SFGs), an extension of CFGs

claim: The compiler includes an analyzer (reachability and dataflow analysis) over VIR.

receipts.text: The analyzer then performs various analyses on the VIR, including reachability analysis and dataflow analysis
